key: Establish worship at the going down of the sun until the dark of night, and (the recital of) the Qur’an at dawn.
s: Turning from those who would drive the Prophet out, the surah gives him the hours of prayer; al-Tabari, on 17:78, takes ‘going down’ as the sun’s leaning past midday, for the noon prayer, and nightfall as the sunset prayer.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 17:78, Tarteel QUL Arabic text via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

opened.edition: Jāmiʿ al-bayān ʿan taʾwīl āy al-Qurʾān, the Tarteel QUL text via spa5k/tafsir_api commit 9ae590a (2026), editors’ footnotes removed
opened.locator: on 17:78, his own heading inside the seg labelled 17:77 to 17:78 (packet.js quran 32 --verse 17.78): his two preferences, on dulūk al-shams and on ghasaq al-layl

evidence.words: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: عنى بقوله ﴿أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ : صلاة الظهر، وذلك أن الدلوك في كلام العرب: الميل … فلا شكّ أن الشمس إذا زالت عن كبد السماء، فقد مالت للغروب، وذلك وقت صلاة الظهر … بإقامتها عند غسق الليل، هي صلاة المغرب دون غيرها، لأن غسق الليل هو ما وصفنا من إقبال الليل وظلامه
evidence.gloss: The more correct of the two sayings is that of those who said that by (Establish prayer at the dulūk of the sun) He meant the noon prayer, because dulūk in the speech of the Arabs is leaning. … There is no doubt that when the sun has passed from the zenith it has leaned towards setting, and that is the time of the noon prayer. … (the prayer he was commanded) to establish at the ghasaq of the night is the sunset prayer and no other, because the ghasaq of the night is, as we described, the night’s coming on and its darkness.

reason: The problem holds. Re-opened packet.js quran 32 --verse 17.78. The digitisation’s seg is labelled 17:77 to 17:78, but inside it al-Tabari opens a separate heading for 17:78 (al-qawl fi taʾwil qawlihi taʿala: aqim al-salat li-duluk al-shams ... (78)). His comment under the 17:77 heading is about God’s way with nations that drive out their messengers and says nothing about prayer. So the place is now ‘on 17:78’ in both s and src, which matches day 13. The src already opened ‘al-Tabari’ in the round-1 revision. All three evidence pieces are verbatim from the packet, joined by ellipses. The middle piece, on the sun passing the zenith, is added so that ‘past midday’ is carried by his own words. Commentator and reading are unchanged. verse.js ok (Al-Isra 17:78, at 2106). entry-check ok.
